reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) shows that hydrogen reduces stacking fault energy and promotes nanotwinning, increasing strength and ductility in the equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEA. However, all evidence is from a single-phase f.c.c. alloy, not the dual-phase eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1, so the transferability premise is unsupported. The hypothesis also assumes the mechanism operates at lamellar colony boundaries, which is not addressed in the cited passages.
premises: Hydrogen reduces stacking fault energy in f.c.c. HEAs
Reduced stacking fault energy promotes deformation nanotwinning
Nanotwinning increases work hardening and delays fracture
Trace hydrogen (tens of ppm) can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in an HEA
These mechanisms are transferable to the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA
